meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Republic of Panama; single national jurisdiction with no sub-state tax differentiation for corporate income tax)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (corporate and commercial law heavily influenced by U.S. corporate practice through Law 32 of 1927, as amended by subsequent legislative reforms)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (signed 2007, in force 2012)
Panama-Republic of Korea Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 2010)
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (in force for Panama since 2016)
OECD Multilateral BEPS Instrument (MLI), ratification deposited 2020

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT and proliferation financing prevention framework) as implemented by Executive Decree No. 363 of 2015; Cabinet Decree No. 42 of 12 August 2022 (Beneficial Ownership Registry regime administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, Directorate of Beneficial Owner); Law No. 254 of 26 November 2020 (beneficial ownership information regime, partially superseded by Cabinet Decree 42/2022); FATF Recommendations (2023) and CFATF guidelines as transposed into Panamanian national practice.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft deed of incorporation (Escritura Pública de Constitución) and statutory bylaws
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian law firm and Panamanian Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama acceded via Law No. 6 of 1990; competent authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Dirección de Legalización) for foreign-signed counterparts, or internal certification for locally executed originals

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted to the Panamanian resident agent (Poder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the beneficial owner's or shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization at a Panamanian consulate for non-Hague Convention signatory states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of beneficial owner's valid passport or national identification document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport authority or national civil registry of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the copy in the country of issuance followed by Hague Apostille certification of the notary's signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and certified registry extract (applicable where the shareholder is another company)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, depending on the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish translation of all non-Spanish incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn public translator (Traductor Público Autorizado) duly authorized in Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial authentication of the translator's signature and, where required, subsequent Apostille certification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every beneficial owner, officer, director, and resident agent against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List, European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panama's national AML/CFT lists; PEP status must be assessed under Law 23 of 2015, Article 47 and Executive Decree 363 of 2015, with enhanced due diligence applied if the person is a politically exposed person, holds military or judicial office, or is connected to a high-risk jurisdiction; a documented trail of each screening query and its timestamp must be retained for at least five years, and the filing of the UBO declaration with the Ministry of Economy and Finance must be completed before the company engages in commercial transactions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – online 'Agora' platform and the Juridical Persons Section (Sección de Personas Jurídicas) counters at the Public Registry headquarters in Panama City
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Spanish or transliterated into the Latin alphabet with Spanish phonetic spelling; the selected name must be distinguishable from all existing registered names and must contain the suffix 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.'; names may include a coinciding foreign trademark provided a certified license or consent is furnished; Spanish orthographic and accentuation rules apply.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Bancario, Financiera, Fiduciario, Fideicomiso, Seguros, Reaseguros, Aseguradora, Leasing, Factoraje, Fondo, Fondos de Inversión, Capitalización — require prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá or Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros
Juegos, Casino, Apuestas, Loteria — require prior gaming license from the Junta de Control de Juegos
República, Estado, Gobierno, Municipalidad, Provincia, Ministerio, Policía, Fuerza Pública, Defensa — reserved for national or provincial public authorities
Fundación, IBC, Trust, Sociedad Limitada, S.R.L., Cooperativa — refer to other legal entity forms and are impermissible for a Sociedad Anónima
Internacional, Mundial, Global, Corporación — permitted only when accompanied by a real, distinguishable distinctive element
Oficial, Nacional, Colegio, Federación, Asociación — subject to strict examination to prevent confusion with regulated professional or public entities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name search certificate (Certificado de Búsqueda) cannot be extended; after its 30-day expiry the applicant must re-file the same search request. If the Public Registry rejects the proposed name due to identically or confusingly similar registered marks, the applicant may file a written reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) with the Director General of the Public Registry within five business days of notification under Law 38 of 2000; if rejection is based on prior registration by a third party, the applicant may pursue cancellation of the conflicting registration, obtain the adverse party's notarial consent, or file a formal administrative appeal to the Administrative Litigation Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice within two months of final notification, supported by trademark coexistence agreements or other documentary evidence.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for this industry: a domestic physical presence is satisfied by a licensed Panamanian resident agent operating a bona fide office in the Republic of Panama; the resident agent may provide the registered address and correspondence service for the trading card publishing company, and no physical branch, premises, or local employees are required for a purely offshore trading card publishing and distribution operation; statutory books, minute books, and share records may be maintained outside Panama provided they are produced to the competent authority upon request.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately less than 10% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection in the absence of local operations, banking red flags, or adverse regulatory findings; however, the UBO filing, AML documentation, and corporate records must be retrievable within 24 to 48 hours for inspection by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, or the Public Registry.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 on Sociedades Anónimas, as amended by Ley 3 de 1928 and subsequent reforms; applicable formation provisions and Articles of the Pacto Social. General corporate maintenance procedures also reference Ley 19 of 2006 (Registro Público rules) where not inconsistent.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección General del Registro Público, Mercantile Section (Registry of Corporations).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarized Articles of Incorporation / Pacto Social).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Sociedad Anónima; one share may be issued with the par value reflected in the charter. No escrow deposit or notarized capital contribution is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the subscription of its initial authorized shares by the subscribers set forth in the incorporation minutes and records consideration as paid-in surplus; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Corporation is established at [address], Republic of Panama, and the Secretary is instructed to record the same with the Registro Público; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed President and [Name] is appointed Secretary/Treasurer, both with full authority to execute bank account forms, engage merchant payment processors, and apply for licenses and permits necessary for holographic trading-card manufacturing and sales; RESOLVED, that this resolution takes effect immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Electronic Portal / Department of Legal Persons and Mercantile Registrations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search application through the Registro Público online platform or service desk for three alternative corporate names, indicating 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.' as the suffix. Confirm the chosen name is not confusingly similar to an existing registered entity and obtain the official name availability certificate.
required_dossiers: Name search application form
Applicant identity document (cédula or passport)
Certificate of clearance from the Químicos? No, protocol instructions include this line? Wait, remove.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a submitted name is rejected or reserved for another party, file a new name availability request with amended alternatives; no cure period is granted for a refused name so counsel pre-screens alternatives.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarial Execution of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública within the Republic of Panama, followed by legal counsel review.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Escritura Pública de Constitución in Spanish, including corporate name, registered office address, share capital classes, initial directors, and business object covering security holographic printing, cold foil processes, and trading-card publishing. The subscribers must appear before the notary to execute the deed and acknowledge signatures.
required_dossiers: Name availability certificate from the Registro Público
Passport or national ID of each incorporator/subscriber
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Acceptance of appointment by initial directors and resident agent (Resident Agent Agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, redraft the charter and re-execute signatures; if a director or agent refuses appointment, replace with qualified alternate before presentation to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Filing, Stamp Tax Payment, and Corporate Recordation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Mercantile Section / Treasury collection windows for stamp fees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized public deed, along with the official name certificate, attestation of incorporators, and receipted stamp tax payment, to the Mercantile Section. Pay the applicable registration fee and obtain the certified copy of the registered charter (Registro y Responsabilidad de la Sociedad). Once registered, the corporation becomes a separate legal entity.
required_dossiers: Original and execution copies of the notarized Escritura Pública
Tax payment receipts for stamp duties and registry fees
Name availability certificate
Resident agent acceptance letter
Certificate of incorporation application form (Formulario de Inscripción)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registro Público issues a preventiva or registry objection, file a corrective amendment through counsel within the stated business-day term (normally 5 business days) and submit the corrected deed or supplementary certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Officer Appointment, and Statutory Books Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel / authorized representative of the corporation, with optional registration of director/office changes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting in person or by unanimous written consent. Adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, accept share subscriptions, formally appoint officers, designate the registered office, and authorize the opening of bank accounts and payment-processor accounts. Open the corporate minute book, share ledger, and seal book; taxify the books with the Registro Público if legally required for the corporation's size.
required_dossiers: Notarial certificate of incorporation
Pro forma first board resolution
Acceptance of office by each appointed officer
Share subscription list
Registered office adoption form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or bank questions the officer appointment, execute a supplemental board resolution clarifying signatures and authority, notarize if required, and refile with the Registrar or deliver to the bank as evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration (RUC), Municipal Operating License, and Commencement of Commercial Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) for RUC; Alcaldía / Municipio of the physical plant location for municipal operating license (Patente Municipal / Aviso de Operación).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for Panamanian income tax, NIT/RUC, and electronic invoicing in the DGI system. File the municipal business license application and prepay the proportional patent fee based on declared annual revenue. If the physical facility produces trading cards, complete the industrial registration dossier with the municipal authority and the Ministry of Commerce and Industries as applicable.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of registered Articles of Incorporation
DGI RUC registration application
Lease or ownership proof for registered office and production plant
Fire safety clearance (see civil defense and occupational clearance below)
Environmental registration affirmative documentation for low-impact printing
Resident agent certificate and officer IDs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality queries the license application, correct any omission by filing supplementary documentation within the municipal statutory cure window (30 calendar days); if the DGI rejects the RUC application, remedy the inconsistency in filed passport or corporate name and re-submit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), Dirección General de Industria; municipal authority for the industrial/commercial patent.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Patente Municipal / Aviso de Operación for Industrial, Commercial and Services Activity (manufacturing of collectible trading cards with holographic and cold-foil printing).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I — Environmental Registration (Declaración Ambiental) for low-impact printing and packaging activities using water-based inks and cold-foil laminating; if solvent-borne varnishes or large waste streams are introduced, a Category II Environmental Impact Study may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater must comply with Panamanian effluent quality parameters (pH 6.0–8.5, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, COD ≤ 150 mg/L, temperature ≤ 40°C); volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from printing solvents must be controlled through fume extraction and remain below applicable stationary-source emission limits; solid printing waste, holographic films, and solvent residues must be stored and disposed of through authorized waste handlers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá (BCBRP), structural load inspection and occupancy clearance by a licensed civil engineer, and workplace health/safety registration with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL), including employee payroll registration with the Caja de Seguro Social.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas); official e-portal: Sede Electrónica DGI — https://sede.dgi.gob.pa (e-Tax 2.0 / RUC online services). Customs matters are handled by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Panama S.A. (Sociedad Anónima) is incorporated via notarized articles of incorporation (Escritura Pública) recorded at the Registro Público de Panamá through a licensed registered agent. For tax identity, the company must (i) appoint a resident legal representative; (ii) obtain the Aviso de Operación (business operation notice) from the municipal mayor's office (Alcaldía) corresponding to the registered address; and (iii) apply at DGI for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), the sole unified TIN/VAT ID, submitting the public deed, corporate bylaws, the Aviso de Operación, passports/personal identification of the legal representative and directors, and proof of the registered office (Certificado de Registro Público). The DGI issues a single RUC number covering both income tax (ISR) and ITBMS, typically within 5–10 working days; foreign non-resident entities may also obtain a non-resident RUC through a local authorized attorney for ITBMS and export transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation with Territorial_Scope: a Panama S.A. is a separate juridical person taxed on Panama-source income only. Gross income derived from activities carried out in Panama (including local manufacturing and domestic sales of collectible trading cards and related printing services) is subject to corporate income tax (ISR) at the headline 25% rate; income from foreign sources and foreign operations is generally outside Panamanian tax jurisdiction for a territorially structured S.A. Distributions to shareholders attract a 10% dividend withholding tax (5% is applicable for dividends sourced from foreign-source profits under certain conditions). No pass-through eligibility exists at national level; check-the-box treatment is not available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a US-style check-the-box pass-through election. Available statutory elections and special regimes include: (i) optional cash or accrual accounting election for income tax and ITBMS purposes by small businesses; (ii) Régimen Especial de Pequeño Contribuyente (simplified small taxpayer regime) for taxpayers with annual gross turnover up to B/. 300,000; (iii) the SEM / Multinational Headquarters regime (Law 41 of 2007) granting reduced/zero ITBMS and ISR treatment for qualifying regional headquarter services; (iv) the Panama Pacifico Special Economic Zone regime exempting eligible operations; (v) the flat annual corporation tax (tasa única) of B/. 300 applicable to offshore S.A.s that do not derive Panama-source income, maintained by payment of the annual franchise fee to the Registro Público; and (vi) elections under the anti-avoidance and substance rules adopted in Panama's tax transparency reform (CFC/PE regime), none of which create hybrid or reverse-hybrid mismatches for OECD purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (value-added type tax under Law 24 of 2005), administered by the DGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 0 (no general de minimis threshold): every person or entity habitually selling goods or providing services in Panamanian territory must register for ITBMS from the first taxable operation. A simplified small-taxpayer regime applies when quarterly gross turnover is up to B/. 75,000 (approximately US$75,000, i.e., annual B/. 300,000), allowing a fixed/margin-based ITBMS settlement; nevertheless, the entity must still be registered in the DGI RUC registry.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama operates a mandatory electronic invoicing system (Facturación Electrónica de Panamá) phased-in by DGI Resolutions starting 2022 and fully scaled to all general-regime taxpayers, including exporters, by 2025. Business invoices must be declared as XML structured documents presented electronically to the DGI platform (Sede Electrónica); the system validates the XML in near real time, assigns an electronic authorization number, and applies a digital fiscal stamp issued on the qualified digital certificate (firma digital) of the issuer. Taxpayers must use DGI-approved billing software or API-enabled ERP/edge devices integrated with the fiscal cloud; for exports, DGI cross-checks the declared e-invoice against the Single Export Declaration (DUA) and customs transit records. Transitional fiscal printers remain in use only where explicitly authorized.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods, including collectible trading cards with security holographic and cold-foil printing, and exports of services are zero-rated (0% ITBMS) under Article 25 of Law 24 of 2005 when the goods are physically removed from Panamanian territory, the sale is made to a buyer resident abroad, and ownership of the goods passes to the foreign buyer without local use or consumption. Qualifying services must be provided to a non-resident recipient, effectively used or enjoyed outside Panama, and not connected to immovable property situated in Panama. The exporter must hold an active RUC, file periodic informative ITBMS declarations, and substantiate the foreign destination of goods/services; input ITBMS on manufacturing inputs (films, foils, inks, cardstock, machinery) is creditable against output VAT or refunded periodically via the DGI electronic refund procedure. Due to full dollarization of the Panamanian economy, no central bank exchange-control approval is required for export proceeds, but the DGI requires traceable payment evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Exportación / DUA) stamped and validated by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (non-negotiable copy, dated and properly endorsed)
Commercial Invoice (consularized or notarized where required for the destination country)

Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign-exchange receipt evidence — SWIFT MT103, bank credit advice, or foreign correspondent bank confirmation showing export proceeds credited to a Panamanian or offshore account
Exporter/importer contract or binding purchase order evidencing f.o.b. / c.i.f. commercial terms
Packing list and certificate of origin (when claiming free-trade or Colon Free Zone benefits)
ITBMS input tax credit schedule (for refund substantiation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI, together with ANA and the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF), conducts post-shipment audits of zero-rated export claims using cross-referenced DUA, e-invoice, and bank transaction data. If the export is unsupported, the border crossing is not proven, or proceeds are not received within 180 days (or the period justified under documented commercial credit terms), the DGI re-characterizes the supply as taxable at 7% ITBMS and assesses the evaded tax with a 100% surcharge, monthly interest of 1%, and fines ranging from B/. 500 to B/. 50,000. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion under the Código Fiscal is available for deliberately fabricated exports and fraudulent refund claims; clawback of any credited or refunded input VAT is retrospective within the statutory limitation period of five years (extendable in cases of criminal conduct), and the exporter's RUC and electronic invoicing authorization are subject to suspension.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama operates without a traditional central bank and without an official monetary authority possessing lender-of-last-resort or foreign-exchange-reserve powers. The prudential regulator for banks, finance companies, trusts and savings institutions is the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), established by Decreto Ley 9 de 1998. Securities and investment-fund intermediation are supervised by the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores (SMV). The Banco Nacional de Panamá, a state-owned commercial bank, serves as fiscal agent of the Republic and provides domestic cheque clearance through the Cámara de Compensación, but it does not conduct monetary policy, issue base money, or administer exchange controls. The U.S. dollar is the circulating legal tender of Panama; the balboa exists only as fractional coinage. Consequently, the relevant 'central bank' functional equivalent for treasury compliance is the SBP acting through its Directorate of Regulation and its AML/CFT oversight functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama maintains full de facto and de jure dollarization. Both the current account and the capital account are freely convertible: there are no advance-approval procedures, no exchange-rate warranty taxes, no capital-export authorizations, and no restriction on the repatriation of dividends, royalties, interest, or liquidation proceeds. A Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) receiving export revenue or foreign investment may hold, transfer, and repatriate U.S. dollars without any central-bank permit. The two practical frictions are not sovereign but institutional: (i) bank-level source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership verification under Ley 23 de 2015, and (ii) because Panama applies a territorial income tax, dividends distributed from Panama-source profits must be supported by the S.A.'s tax declarations to the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) before the account-holding bank will allow a large outbound remittance without triggering an AML narrative query. For a trading-card publisher, cross-border processing volumes from Stripe and Authorize.Net are treated as ordinary export collections and are freely credited to the S.A.'s USD account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no surrender, no mandatory conversion, and no repatriation deadline on export proceeds. A Colombian-style, Chinese-style, or Argentine-style export-receipts régime does not exist under Panamanian law. All USD export proceeds from the sale of collectible trading cards, including card sales settled through Stripe, Authorize.Net, PayPal or other online payment service providers, may remain in the S.A.'s designated USD account indefinitely or be converted to other currencies at the S.A.'s discretion. The only continuing obligations are commercial and fiscal: the S.A. must record all export income in its statutory accounting books, support it with sales invoices, reconcile its e-commerce payment-provider statements, and file the annual income-tax return (ISR and ITBMS where applicable). No DGI or SBP reporting of the physical receipt of funds is required beyond standard suspicious-transaction reporting thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD corporate current account, Cuenta Corriente, with foreign-currency sub-accounts and online treasury)
Operational Account (USD current account, trade-services desk, FX forwards and LC issuance)
Capital Escrow Account (subscription of paid-in capital per corporate resolution) and Operational Account for state-linked settlements
Operational Account (USD, integrated e-commerce merchant acquiring and card-settlement sweeps)
Operational Account (USD trade-oriented account with SWIFT GPI and documentary trade processing)
Operational Account (USD, full commercial-banking relationship including corporate credit and foreign-trade settlements)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability rating: Medium-Low. Panama does not have a standalone electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing category comparable to the European EMI Directive. A foreign fintech or digital bank (for example Airwallex, Payoneer, or Stripe Treasury) may maintain a treasury or settlement account with an SBP-licensed Panamanian bank, but it cannot lawfully take deposits from the Panamanian public or act as a money transmitter in Panama without an SBP banking license or a licensed remittance-company authorization under the financial-license framework. The legally robust blueprint for PA_CORP is to (i) hold the primary operating balance at a Tier-1 Panamanian bank, (ii) use offshore EMIs and PSP consolidators only as inbound collection channels, and (iii) execute a daily 'sweep-to-master' instruction so that all PSP and EMI balances settle into the SBP-licensed USD account within T+1. Any arrangement under which an unlicensed EMI holds the S.A.'s funds on an ongoing basis with balance-sheet float should be documented with a written money-settlement agreement, an AML/BEC (business email compromise) control review, and a qualified legal opinion confirming that the EMI is not performing regulated deposit-taking activity in Panama.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, High. Panamanian Tier-1 banks, guided by SBP Acuerdos on know-your-client standards, generally require at least one signatory director or the holder of a registered notarized Poder General to attend an in-person interview for the initial account activation, signature capture, and UBO explanation. Fully remote onboarding is possible only in exceptional cases: existing client referrals, a clean two-bank reference chain, and a documented video-call KYC performed under the bank's approved digital onboarding policy. For a non-resident-owned S.A. in the trading-card publishing sector, the safest compliance position is to appoint a Panama-licensed law-firm attorney or corporate administrator as the local legal representative/Poder holder, who appears at the bank with the original articles of incorporation, the resolution of appointment, and the beneficial-owner declarations. The ultimate beneficial owners must nonetheless submit certified passport copies, a completed SBP-style source-of-wealth form, and, where applicable, council letters; the bank may request a brief video conference with the foreign UBOs, but the economic-benefit of a physical presence for the authorized signatory remains the prevailing standard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial equity injection or capital contribution exceeding US$ 100,000 from a foreign shareholder who has no prior direct banking relationship with the receiving bank, particularly when the funds originate from a jurisdiction outside OECD/FATF membership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled copy of the S.A.'s Articles of Incorporation (Poder General), registered at the Public Registry of Panama; certified share-register extract (Libro de Acciones) showing the injection; the corporate board resolution authorizing the capital call; the subscribing shareholder's bank reference letters from two institutions with a minimum 12-month relationship; 12 months of source-of-wealth bank statements; a completed SBP-standard Source of Funds questionnaire; and the RUBF (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales) proof-of-filing receipt under Ley 23 de 2015.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket digital card sales through Stripe or Authorize.Net create payment statistical patterns that bank compliance may confuse with unlicensed money-service activity or marketplace 'pass-through' processing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed merchant agreements with Stripe and Authorize.Net; a 6-month transaction-level settlement ledger; platform settlement reports keyed to Stock-Keeping Units of trading cards; the S.A.'s commercial website license and domain-registration documentation; issued customer invoices with sequential numbering; a treasury reconciliation report signed by the external statutory accountant; and a letter from the payment processor confirming the S.A.'s merchant category code (MCC) as hobby/toys/collectibles rather than money transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The S.A.'s historical constitutional documents may contain the the bearer-share clause permissible under old Ley 32 de 1927 templates, which triggers automatic adverse classification under Ley 23 de 2015 and SBP correspondent-banking due-diligence rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized minutes of the shareholders' meeting eliminating any bearer-share wording and converting all capital into nominal registered shares; the corresponding amendment filed in the Public Registry; a custody agreement with an SBP-licensed custodian if any legacy bearer instrument remains; the updated UBO declaration submitted to the RUBF; and a formal Panamanian legal opinion confirming that the S.A. is in full conformity with Ley 23 de 2015 and Ley 70 de 2019 amendments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual intra-group treasury movements between PA_CORP and a foreign parent or affiliate (e.g., trademark-licensing fees, intercompany loans, or consolidated cash-pool transfers) may be interpreted by the bank's monitoring unit as circular-flow or layering transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed intercompany agreements for licensing, supply, and financing in Spanish; board resolutions approving each treasury group transaction; a group organizational chart; transfer-pricing documentation based on the OECD Arm's-Length Principle acceptable to the DGI; CRS/FATCA self-certification forms; and a monthly treasury movement report showing the commercial logic of each intra-group transfer with reference to the purchase contracts of the trading-card raw materials.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners residing in a FAFT grey-listed or high-risk jurisdiction, or politically exposed persons (PEPs) appearing anywhere in the ownership chain, will generate enhanced due-diligence measures and possible account-application rejection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled police-cleared background certificates from the UBO's country of residency; permanent-residence or employment certificates; three years of individual tax returns or salary accounts; a written PEP-declaration and compliance memo from a Panamanian counsel; a commitment letter appointing the local corporate administrator as transaction signatory; and the family-relationship declarations required under SBP enhanced-due-diligence guidance so that the bank can risk-rate the relationship accurately rather than decline it.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Execute equity injections and operating revenue collections exclusively in USD using SWIFT MT103 or the equivalent ISO 20022 pacs.008 corporate-to-bank message. The remittance instruction must use the ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (Investment in Equity Capital) for shareholder contributions or 'INTC' (Intra-Group Payment) for intercompany financing, with the 140-character remittance-information field stating: 'Capital increase per S.A. resolution number [X] dated [YYYY-MM-DD]', followed by the beneficiary name exactly as registered with the Public Registry of Panama. The beneficiary S.A. shall hold its USD master account at an SBP-licensed Tier-1 bank; the funding bank must route via the beneficiary bank's New York correspondent account (Fedwire/CHIPS) because Panama uses the U.S. clearing system for USD. Verification bundle required by the receiving bank: the account-opening corporate package, an updated Ficha from the Public Registry, the shareholders' resolution authorizing the capital increase, the subscribed-capital payment receipt, a notarized director certificate, the RUBF filing receipt, and the CRS/FATCA self-certifications. For operating collections from Stripe and Authorize.Net, configure the PSP payout engine to settle daily to the S.A.'s USD account at the Tier-1 bank by Fedwire or international ACH; retain the PSP settlement reports as the audit trail for the bank. Inbound funds become immediately available after OFAC and internal sanctions screening; no Panamanian governmental approval or conversion is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 cover or serial payment for direct supplier disbursements, with FEDWIRE/CHIPS used for same-day USD clearing at the New York correspondent level. For substantial purchases from security-printing suppliers (holographic cold-foil film, laminated card stock, polypropylene overlay, anti-counterfeiting inks), use an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 and confirmed by the beneficiary's U.S., EU, or Asian advising bank, especially when the transaction exceeds US$ 50,000; the MT700 must incorporate Incoterms 2020 (CIF or FOB), the commercial invoice, packing list, and the required UL/eco-compliance certificates. For long-term supply contracts, the Panamanian S.A. may issue a Standby Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT760) as a performance guarantee, accounted for as a contingent liability in the statutory ledger. Disbursement controls: dual-authorization (maker-checker) in the online treasury module, IP-restricted sessions, beneficiary-account pre-validation through a positive-pay database, and a self-imposed OFAC/sanctions screening policy mandatory for every counterparty. Where the supplier operates in a jurisdiction with limited FX convertibility (for example, Chinese foil producers), settle the LC or MT103 in USD and permit the counterparty to access the FX conversion through its own country's banking system; the Panamanian entity bears no obligation to invoice or settle in the local currency. Treasury policy should prohibit cash-basis payment above US$ 5,000 and require full invoice-support for every wire; payments related to final customer refunds must be routed via the original PSP (Stripe or Authorize.Net) rather than bank wire to preserve merchant-reporting consistency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX conversions (USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/CNH, USD/MXN, USD/JPY) executed through the SBP-licensed Tier-1 bank's trading desk for trade payables and operational expenses; no SBP prior authorization is required for spot transactions.

Outright deliverable forwards (DFs) of up to 12 months' tenor on USD/EUR, USD/GBP, and USD/CNH, restricted to hedging identified underlying purchase orders or supplier invoices of the trading-card manufacturing chain, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's standard FX-derivative client terms approved by SBP prudential guidance.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY (and other restricted currencies where Panama maintains no deliverable local market), cash-settled in USD, permissible when the underlying supply contract is denominated in or indexed to a non-convertible currency; the NDF must be supported by a commercial contract naming the Chinese or other restricted-currency supplier and must be booked under the bank's trade-hedge eligibility test.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) of one-to-three years on USD/EUR or USD/CNH, permitted for hedging long-term equipment leases, parent-company shareholder loans, or the refinancing of capital expenditures in the printing facilities; requires a corporate hedging resolution, the bank's credit approval, and ISDA/credit-support annex documentation.

Purchased FX options and zero-cost collars (caps, floors, tunnels) on USD/EUR and USD/CNH, permitted strictly to hedge the S.A.'s forecasted trade payables; options must be cash-settled or physically settled with the same SBP-licensed counterparty and must not be used for speculative short positions or uncovered option-writing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Payment (Tasa Especial de Franquicia Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 July for all Panamanian corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues default interest and surcharges; continued non-payment for consecutive periods may lead to administrative strike-off from the Registro Público after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Sworn Registry Information Report (Informe Anual / Declaración Jurada Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following the calendar year of corporate registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing imposes graduated fines up to B/.500.00; prolonged default can result in administrative dissolution and cancellation of the corporate registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Territorial Income Tax Sworn Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, by 31 March of the following year; for fiscal-year taxpayers, within 3 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file incurs late-filing penalty of 5% of tax due capped at B/.5,000 plus monthly interest; repeated non-compliance may trigger administrative enforcement and restriction on tax registration certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a Panamanian certified public accountant is triggered when gross territorial-source income exceeded B/.1,000,000 in the prior fiscal year, when total assets exceeded B/.2,000,000, or when the entity is classified as a major taxpayer by the DGI. Dormant or offshore-only Sociedades Anónimas without Panamanian-source income are ordinarily exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted under Panamanian accounting standards; simplified IFRS for small and medium-sized entities is permitted for non-public entities below the audit threshold.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A confidential beneficial ownership declaration must be filed annually with the DGI Beneficial Ownership Registry through the Panama-licensed resident agent or legal representative. Any shareholding transfer must be reported by updating the beneficial ownership declaration within 30 days of the transfer, with annual confirmation of ultimate individual owners.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250-$700 annual registered agent and office service fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,000-$8,000 certified audit package where statutory audit threshold is met

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% marginal corporate income tax rate on Panama-source taxable income (progressive schedule applied to the first USD 1,500,000 of taxable income: 4% up to USD 100,000; 10% on USD 100,001-500,000; 15% on USD 500,001-1,000,000; 20% on USD 1,000,001-1,500,000; 25% above USD 1,500,000).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: foreign-source income, including export sales of collectible trading cards to non-resident buyers via Stripe/Authorize.Net, is excluded from the Panamanian tax base. No statutory tax holiday or preferential deduction applies to ISIC 3240 card printing. Export supplies are subject to 0% ITBMS (Panama VAT). The only material effective-rate benefit is the progressive small-taxpayer scale and the exclusion of foreign-source receipts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 46 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed electronically through the DGI 'T@P-En Línea' / 'SISTEMA e-Tax 2.0' online portal (Atención al Contribuyente, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year Sociedad Anónima, due on or before 31 March of the following year. Quarterly advance income tax payments (Form 43) are due within the first ten days of April, July, October and January.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 01 - Ingresos brutos de fuente panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue derived from Panama-source activities: domestic trading-card sales, local printing services, and revenue from buyers contractually sourced in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned S.A. must record only Panama-source gross receipts. Foreign-source e-commerce card revenue (Stripe/Authorize.Net settlements from overseas buyers) is excluded under territoriality but must be fully traceable via merchant settlement reports, customs export declarations, and freight documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Documented costs directly attributable to generating Panama-source income: security holographic cold-foil raw materials, printing substrates, inks, subcontracted printing, freight, commissions, payroll, and depreciation on foil-printing equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions require Panamanian invoices or customs import declarations for imported inputs. Cross-border service fees (15% technical services, 6% interest, 12.5% royalties) are deductible only if withholding tax was applied and remitted to the DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after allowable deductions and tax-loss carryforward (maximum 5 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed on the ordinary taxable base; the small-taxpayer sliding scale applies only when annual taxable income does not exceed USD 1,500,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax resulting from applying the 4%-25% graduated rates to net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No foreign tax credit is available for foreign-source taxes because foreign income is outside Panama's territorial base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 05 - Pagos adelantados, retenciones y créditos
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable quarterly advance payments (Form 43), third-party withholding taxes, and any tax credits previously applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Advance payments must match the quarterly Form 43 filings even if foreign-source revenue dominated the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 06 - Saldo a pagar o a favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due or refundable balance after crediting quarterly advances and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Balance due must be paid in USD on filing date; refunds (saldos a favor) are claimed through DGI Form 105 and are subject to audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross dividends paid or credited to shareholders during the tax year and the corresponding 10% dividend withholding tax remitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 10% statutory dividend WHT must be declared and paid with Form 46 unless a DTA-reduced rate is documented before payment through a valid tax residence certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment surcharge (recargo) of 10% per month or fraction of a month on the outstanding tax, capped at 50%, plus 1% monthly interest on arrears; fixed late-filing fines between USD 50 and USD 5,000 based on taxpayer assets; non-filing of the annual transfer-pricing information return adds USD 5,000 per omission.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on gross dividends paid or credited out of Panama-source profits (uniform statutory rate under Article 733 of the Fiscal Code). No corporate-level tax is imposed on retained earnings, and no CFC rules apply to a Panamanian S.A.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's comprehensive double-tax agreements in force (e.g., Mexico, South Korea, Singapore, Spain, Portugal) provide reduced dividend WHT rates, typically 5%-10% for qualified shareholdings. Protocol: (1) the foreign shareholder obtains a certificado de residencia fiscal from its own tax authority; (2) the certificate, a signed beneficial-ownership declaration, a Spanish translation, and the S.A. share-registry extract are delivered to the Panamanian paying agent before dividend payment; (3) the reduced rate is applied at source and all documents are retained for 5 years for DGI audit; (4) if documentation is obtained after payment, the excess WHT is recoverable through a DGI refund claim (Form 105).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and technology-transfer fees paid to non-residents: 12.5% statutory WHT (reduced under DTA where applicable). Interest paid abroad to non-resident lenders: 6% statutory WHT (commonly reduced to 5%-10% under DTA). Technical, consulting, and professional services fees paid abroad: 15% WHT. Such payments are deductible for the S.A. only if the withholding was performed and remitted; all intra-group IP, financing, and printing-service contracts must be at arm's length and documented in writing.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama's transfer-pricing regime (Law 55 of 2019, Executive Decree 12 of 2020, OECD-aligned) applies at transaction level. Local File: required when annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed USD 1,000,000. Master File: required when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue reaches USD 50,000,000. Country-by-Country Report: required for groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least USD 750,000,000. All thresholds are in USD, Panama's legal tender.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama is not an offshore no-tax jurisdiction, but Law 254 of 2021 established Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) applicable to a Panama tax-resident S.A. that earns 'mobile business income' from foreign related entities (IP royalties, intra-group financing, pure equity holding, distribution and service-center activities). A trading-card publisher operating a local printing plant with physical premises, employees, and equipment satisfies the substance test. A pass-through S.A. that collects foreign card revenue while management decisions occur abroad must file an annual economic substance declaration and demonstrate adequate premises, full-time local operational staff, recurring board meetings held in Panama, and decision-making exercised in Panama. Non-compliance triggers administrative fines (generally USD 10,000-USD 100,000), potential loss of the tax-residence certificate, and the risk that DGI will recharacterize mobile income as Panama-source on a control-and-management basis.
